text:
Alyssa: Hey team — after I rebased feature/fast-kv onto main and squashed my WIP commits, CI turned red on the runtime/compiler unit tests. Can someone help triage? CI failure looks like an assertion in kv_cache.cc.

ci-bot: build failed · linux-x86_64 · job=unit-runtime-compiler · status=FAILED · https://ci/internal/1793008881

Ben: ugh, did you resolve conflicts manually or use our rebase script?

Alyssa: manual resolve, there was one conflict in kv_cache.h (common header). I thought I kept the new cache invalidation change.

Sofia: can you paste the failing test name / stack? sometimes rebases drop a macro or an include.

Alyssa: failing test is RuntimeKV.CacheEvictionSmoke. Here's the top of the junit log:```
[ RUN      ] RuntimeKV.CacheEvictionSmoke
../../redwood/runtime/kv_cache.cc:412: void redwood::kv::Cache::evict_prefix(const Key&): Assertion `entries_.size() <= capacity_' failed.
#0 0x7f8c... (libpthread)
#1 0x55aa... (kv_cache.cc:412)
```

Raj: That assertion suggests capacity_ is zero or tiny. Any chance a config default changed in main recently? We had a default-capacity tweak in 1789000000.

Ben: I rebased main into my branch yesterday and saw compilation warnings about a removed DEFAULT_KV_CAPACITY. If Alyssa's squash dropped the new initializer, capacity_ could be uninitialized on some platforms.

Alyssa: oh crap — I remember resolving a small initializer conflict manually. Will check the diff.

Sofia: before digging too deep, can you try a targeted rerun for the failing job? If it's flaky we can rerun quick.

ci-bot: rerun requested by Sofia · job=unit-runtime-compiler · queued

ci-bot: rerun started · job=unit-runtime-compiler · run=1793008899

ci-bot: rerun finished · job=unit-runtime-compiler · status=FAILED · run=1793008899

Alyssa: rerun still failed. Reproduces locally for me with `./bazel test //runtime:kv_test --test_arg=CacheEvictionSmoke`.

Raj: can you run with ASAN or with a print to confirm capacity_ value right before eviction? e.g.:```
// temporarily in kv_cache.cc
printf("capacity=%zu entries=%zu\n", capacity_, entries_.size());
```

Alyssa: added print, repro locally: capacity=0 entries=3. So initializer not applied.

Ben: ok that matches my suspicion. In main we moved DEFAULT_KV_CAPACITY into config/defaults.h and switched to `config::default_kv_capacity()` in the constructor. If your constructor still uses `DEFAULT_KV_CAPACITY` macro but the header include got lost, it could become 0 on some compilers due to a macro being undefined.

Sofia: easiest fix: check commit that touched kv_cache ctor in your branch vs main. If you prefer, run `git diff main -- runtime/kv_cache.cc` and look for constructor change.

Alyssa: running diff now... I see in my branch ctor was edited during rebase, the initializer list is `capacity_(0)` — guess I overwrote it trying to resolve conflict. Sorry.

Raj: that explains it. Can you open a quick PR with the restore plus a tiny unit test to catch zero-capacity regressions? Then we can request a fast-track review.

Alyssa: will do. Pushing fix shortly. Patch:```
- Cache::Cache() : capacity_(0) { }
+ Cache::Cache() : capacity_(config::default_kv_capacity()) { }
```

Ben: also add a comment to avoid future squash-rebase mistakes: `// keep in sync with config/defaults.h`

Alyssa: pushed 1793009022-fix-kv-capacity-restore. Created PR and requested Ben for review.

ci-bot: new commit pushed to branch feature/fast-kv · commit=3f7a9e2 · status=CI_PENDING

ci-bot: job=unit-runtime-compiler · run=1793009155 · status=FAILED (flake?)

Sofia: interesting — new run still failed but logs show the fix applied then another test hit a timeout. Could be unrelated flakiness.

Raj: can you rerun only the failing test group with `--test_filter=RuntimeKV.*` to narrow it down?

Alyssa: rerunning targeted job now. If it passes locally but fails in CI's gcc-11 worker, we might have an ABI or builder image mismatch.

ci-bot: targeted run started · filter=RuntimeKV.* · run=1793009201

ci-bot: targeted run finished · status=PASSED · run=1793009201

Alyssa: targeted passed in CI. Looks like previous failure was a flake/timebox. The full job still failed earlier due to a slow integration test hitting 5m timeout.

Ben: okay closing this thread — root cause was the bad manual rebase that set capacity_ to 0. Good catch. Add a tiny test to prevent accidental zero-capacity and maybe land the comment. :thumbsup:

Sofia: rebase note: prefer `git rebase --onto` or use our rebase-helper script to preserve initializers. Learned that the hard way.

Alyssa: thanks all. Will merge after CI green. cc @everyone if you want to review the PR.
